Effect of Saccharin on Crystallization Behavior of
Electroless Cobalt Plating
Yu-Xin Luo<sup>#</sup>, Jing-Jing Wang<sup>#</sup>, Lu Wang, Zi-Yi Yan, Yi Ma, Xin Bo*, Jing-Shuang Dang*,
Zeng-Lin Wang*
Key Laboratory of Applied Surface and Colloid Chemistry, Ministry of Education; Institute of New Concept Sensors and Molecular
Materials; School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering; Shaanxi Normal University; Xi’an, Shaanxi, China, 710119
Abstract
In the process of electroless cobalt plating, the saccharin additive can significantly change the surface morphology, texture
orientation, and conductivity of the cobalt coating layer. When the amount of saccharin was 3 mg·L<sup>–1</sup>, the cobalt coating
transformed from disordered large grains to a honeycomb structure, with a preferred orientation of (002) facet on hexago-

10.7 μΩ·cm after the annealing treatment. When the concentration of saccharin was increased, the grain size was gradually
refined and a “stone forest” structure was observed, with the preferred orientation remaining unchanged. The addition of
saccharin also slightly improves the purity of cobalt coating to a certain extent. Through the study of the crystallization
behavior of cobalt electroless plating, saccharin molecules can adsorb to specific c-sites on the cobalt dense crystal plane,
inhibiting the growth of abc stacking arrangement and inducing the crystal growth in ab stacking mode, thereby achieving
optimal growth of HCP (002) texture.

increased power consumption, which in turn affects
the computing speed and overall device performance

a barrier layer of approximately 2 nm tantalum ni-
tride (TaN) to prevent copper metal from diffusing
into the silicon dielectric layer, thus further increas-

with semiconductor manufacturing, which has been
considered as a new type of interconnect material to

to adopt cobalt as a new interconnect metal for ad-

balt super-filling in chip microholes [9–11], compared
with electrodeposited copper, electrodeposited cobalt
is prone to forming holes and cracks due to such is-
sues as hydrogen evolution, homogenization and
poor coating quality [12]. Electroless plating is one of
the most practical routs to realize cobalt plating in in-
dustrial-scale since it presents a good coverage abil-
ity, facile processing and low cost. Particularly, addi-
tives play a crucial role in electroless plating [13–16].
The appropriate additives not only can improve the
quality of the chemical coating, but also enhance its

Saccharin (SAC) is a common organic, non-toxic
small molecule that can be used as an additive in the elec-
troplating process to improve the quality of coatings,
reduce internal stress, refine grains, enhance the gloss-
iness and reflectivity of coatings [17–19]. Altamirano-
Garcia et al. [20] studied the effects of sulfates, chlo-
rides, and saccharin on the electrodeposition of
cobalt nickel alloys, and found that the addition of
saccharin significantly improved the deposition cur-
rent efficiency and suppressed hydrogen production,
thereby improving the density of the alloy coating.
Hoghoghifard et al. successfully improved the micro-
wave absorption performance of nickel coated fabrics
by adding saccharin to the plating solution [21]. They
found that adding saccharin can reduce surface resis-
tivity, refine grain size, enhance hysteresis loss, and
ultimately improve the microwave shielding effect of
the fabric. Kolonits et al. found that adding saccharin
can significantly refine grain size, increase lattice de-
fect density, and thus improve the hardness of nickel
films [22]. Currently, researchers explored the additive
mechanism through molecular dynamics simulations
and calculations of quantum chemistry, which can
effectively resolve molecular-metal interactions [23,
24]. Nevertheless, the researches on quantum chemi-
cal calculation of the electroless cobalt plating under
the influence of additives are insufficient. Therefore,
it is of great significance to establish a method based
on quantum chemical calculation to study the effect
of additives on cobalt plating.
Upon electroless cobalt plating, we observed that
the addition of saccharin would change the morphol-
ogy of cobalt plating. Then we systematically studied
the effects of saccharin additive on the microstruc-
ture, crystallization behavior, and conductivity of co-
balt plating. It was found that adding an appropriate
amount of saccharin can effectively adsorb specific
crystal planes of cobalt crystals, thereby directionally
regulating their growth behavior and obtaining co-
balt coatings with (002) texture preferred orientation,
which promotes the conductivity of cobalt coatings.
At the same time, density functional theory (DFT)
simulations provided insights into the crystallization
behavior of cobalt coatings, revealing that saccharin
molecules can adsorb to specific sites on the cobalt
dense crystal plane, blocking abc packing and induc-
ing crystal growth in ab stacking mode to form hex-
agonal close-packed structure (002) texture.

4. Conclusions
In the process of electroless cobalt plating, the ad-
dition of saccharin changes the microstructure of the
obtained cobalt layer. The addition of a small amount
of saccharin at a concentration of 3 mg·L<sup>–1</sup> caused the
cobalt plating film to change from disordered orien-
tation to hexagonal texture, with the preferred ori-
entation of (002) facet of HCP Co phase. Continuous
increase in the saccharin concentration (>200 mg·L<sup>–1</sup>)
resulted in the refinement of cobalt film grains with
a “Stone Forest” morphology. The honeycomb mor-
phologic cobalt coating with the appropriate addition
of saccharin (3 mg·L<sup>–1</sup>) presented a tight grain bound-
ary connection, thereby reducing the resistance to
10.7 μΩ·cm. After studying the cobalt crystalliza-
tion process and conducting DFT simulations, it is
found that the charge density near the aromatic ring
of saccharin is increased from the Co surface dona-
tion, so that the saccharin molecules can adsorb to
specific c-sites on the surface of densely packed co-
balt atoms, hindering the abc stacking arrangement.
The crystallization process can be tuned to proceed
along the ab stacking, thus forming the (002) pre-
ferred texture of HCP cobalt. The findings from this
study not only provide a detailed understanding
of the role of saccharin in electroless cobalt plating,
but also offer a theoretical framework for the design
and optimization of additives in electroless plating
processes.

罗雨欣#， 王静静#，王露，闫子一， 马艺，薄鑫*， 党静霜*， 王增林*
陕西师范大学， 化学化工学院， 新概念传感器与分子研究院， 应用表面与胶体化学教育部重点实验室，
陕西，西安， 710119， 中国
摘要：
在化学镀钴过程中， 我们发现添加剂糖精的加入可明显改变化学镀钴层表面的形貌、 织构取向及镀
层的导电性。 研究表明， 当糖精添加量为
3 \mathrm { m g } { \cdot } \mathrm { L } ^ { - 1 }
时， 钴镀层由无序大晶粒转变为蜂巢状结构， 具有密
排六方 （HCP） 钴晶体的 （002） 择优取向， 其电阻率降低至
1 4 . 4 \mu \Omega \cdot \mathrm { c m }
， 经过热处理后， 电阻率进一步
降低至
1 0 . 7 ~ \mu \Omega \cdot \mathrm { c m }
， 这对于其在芯片中的应用具有重要价值。 当糖精浓度升高时， 晶粒逐渐细化， 呈
现 “石林” 状结构， 择优取向不变， 而糖精的加入在一定程度上提高了镀钴膜的纯度。 通过密度泛函理
论对钴镀层结晶行为的研究表明， 糖精分子可吸附于钴密排晶面的特定 c 位点， 抑制 abc 堆积方式生
长， 诱导晶体按 ab 堆积方式生长， 从而实现 HCP（002） 晶面的择优生长。
关键词：化学镀钴； 添加剂； 糖精； 结晶行为
